ask: Users want durable cross-session knowledge that stays relevant.
plugin: A memory skill and MCP store record approved facts, retrieve them on SessionStart, and prune stale entries.

ask: Users want concurrent sessions to avoid colliding on repositories and worktrees.
plugin: SessionStart and SessionEnd hooks maintain a process-aware lock registry and warn or block conflicting sessions.

ask: Users want to check or redact assistant prose before it is shown or transmitted.
plugin: An experimental response middleware checks text against configurable rules and requests revision or redaction before display.

ask: Users want factual or completion claims backed by actual tool evidence.
plugin: A Stop hook or experimental response middleware tracks verification events, checks claims, and requires a readback before final answers.

ask: Users want required skills and procedures applied before matching work.
plugin: A PreToolUse hook matches paths and operations, loads the governing skill, and blocks work until prerequisites are acknowledged.

ask: Users want agents to stay within an approved plan and avoid unauthorized actions.
plugin: Hooks compare proposed tool calls and edits with an approved scope ledger, then block or ask for expansion.

ask: Users want sensitive data and dangerous commands caught before execution or commit.
plugin: PreToolUse and git hooks scan command inputs, diffs, and files for credentials and risky operations.

ask: Users want evidence that hooks are registered, firing, and enforcing decisions.
plugin: A diagnostic command and hooks log registration, event receipts, allow/deny outcomes, and fail-open conditions.

ask: Users want third-party plugins assessed for malicious or surprising behavior.
plugin: A local audit command inspects plugin manifests, hooks, scripts, permissions, and network calls before activation or updates.

ask: Users want plugin caches, versions, and update health maintained automatically.
plugin: A bin command checks resolved versions, cleans orphaned caches, and reports stale installs; a startup hook can prompt for safe updates.

ask: Users want skills surfaced at the right time without filling the context window.
plugin: A routing skill and lightweight index select relevant skills and defer large references until invoked.

ask: Users want skills triggered by events, paths, aliases, or multiple languages.
plugin: A settings hook matches prompts and tool paths against a configurable routing table, then injects the matching skill guidance.

ask: Users want skill definitions tested and corrected before release.
plugin: A command validates frontmatter, trigger examples, permissions, references, and cross-platform scripts with realistic eval cases.

ask: Users want local or team variants of shared skills without forking the original.
plugin: A skill loader hook composes a shared skill with project, user, or team overlays and records precedence.

ask: Users want to inspect, enable, and distinguish available skills and plugins.
plugin: A command enumerates resolved skills, sources, versions, namespaces, and enabled state with searchable output.

ask: Users want costly skill or workflow invocations estimated and approved.
plugin: A skill wrapper estimates agent and token cost, selects a budget, and asks before expensive fan-out.

ask: Users want visibility and control over context consumption and compaction.
plugin: A statusline and hook estimate tokens, identify heavy context entries, and prompt for safe summarization or a fresh session.

ask: Users want to control what context survives compaction.
plugin: Experimental session.compact middleware prioritizes project state, skill decisions, and essential transcript facts.

ask: Users want programmatic, consistent session names and tab labels.
plugin: A SessionStart hook or function hook derives names from project/task metadata and updates the session title.

ask: Users want predictable setup and cleanup for worktree sessions.
plugin: WorktreeCreate, EnterWorktree, and WorktreeRemove hooks set up dependencies, track roots, and clean state.

ask: Users want hooks and workflows to know when background tasks finish or stall.
plugin: A monitor tracks spawned processes and agent receipts, exposes liveness, and blocks premature completion.

ask: Users want limits on recursive subagents and per-agent resource use.
plugin: A PreToolUse Agent hook keeps a spawn ledger, caps depth and spend, and surfaces per-agent usage.

ask: Users want task-specific model and effort choices for skills and agents.
plugin: A skill or experimental tool middleware routes task types to chosen models and effort levels, with a cost cap.

ask: Users want permission decisions and reasons available to hooks and audits.
plugin: PermissionRequest and PermissionDenied hooks log per-call decisions and correlate them with tool IDs; function hooks fill missing lifecycle data.

ask: Users want hook output and assistant progress displayed clearly.
plugin: An output style and statusline present progress, hook notices, and linked messages in a consistent readable format.

ask: Users want a reliable review of the actual proposed change before submission.
plugin: A review skill resolves the correct base and scope, runs independent checks, and verifies findings before posting.

ask: Users want code review to finish within a selected effort and token budget.
plugin: A review command selects agent count and model, tracks progress, and stops or resumes before the budget is exhausted.

ask: Users want research that checks primary sources and produces a complete report.
plugin: A research skill orchestrates search, source capture, verification, and synthesis with checkpointed progress.

ask: Users want repository-grounded insights in useful formats and time ranges.
plugin: A command analyzes local sessions and repository evidence, then generates HTML or text reports with locale and timespan options.

ask: Users want design-system checks and scaffolds across frameworks without destructive edits.
plugin: A design-sync skill adapts component discovery, preview, and validation to the project framework and requires diff approval before rewrites.

ask: Users want messaging channels to reliably relay inbound messages and replies.
plugin: An MCP channel server normalizes messages, queues them durably, and handles replies and reconnects.

ask: Users want more Slack message actions from Claude.
plugin: An MCP server exposes pin, unpin, mark-read, and workflow-trigger tools.

ask: Users want inbound channel content treated safely and with proper identity.
plugin: A channel MCP server escapes content, attaches sender provenance, and can filter or quarantine suspicious messages.

ask: Users want portable plugin hook scripts on Windows, WSL, macOS, Linux, and NixOS.
plugin: A bin launcher selects native interpreters, quotes paths, and provides platform-specific wrappers with self-tests.

ask: Users want plugin options and credentials consumable by skills and scripts.
plugin: A configuration skill and wrapper read userConfig through supported placeholders or environment variables and pass only scoped values to scripts.

ask: Users want plugin packages checked against runtime behavior before release.
plugin: A command validates manifests, files, references, tools, hooks, and packaging with targeted runtime smoke tests.

ask: Users want dependency changes kept lean and safe.
plugin: A PostToolUse hook compares package manifests and lockfiles against size, license, and vulnerability policy.

ask: Users want commits checked for content and message quality before publishing.
plugin: A git hook and review skill inspect staged changes, suggest a better message, and require an explicit review receipt.

ask: Users want dynamic custom slash commands, suggestions, and argument completion.
plugin: A function hook registers commands and live completion providers backed by project data.

ask: Users want sessions started, continued, and finalized through plugin-defined workflows.
plugin: A command plus lifecycle hooks implement session startup guidance, checkpoints, and clean handoff.

ask: Users want tool results or errors redacted, shortened, or repaired before the model sees them.
plugin: PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure hooks transform results where supported; function hooks handle remaining internal cases.

ask: Users want submitted prompts edited or screened before the model sees them.
plugin: An experimental prompt middleware can replace prompt text, attach policy context, or route the turn.

ask: Users want to inspect available tools and adapt workflows to capability changes.
plugin: A function hook enumerates tools and schemas, then exposes a diagnostic command and compatibility checks.

ask: Users want plugin-carried instructions and path rules applied reliably in projects.
plugin: A SessionStart hook imports versioned guidance from the plugin root and checks path-scoped activation.

ask: Users want new hook points for lifecycle and UI events.
plugin: Experimental function hooks instrument missing events and emit plugin-defined callbacks.

ask: Users want richer metadata in hook inputs.
plugin: Experimental function hooks attach the active skill, model, agent, usage, tool input, and task identity to event payloads.

ask: Users want hooks to rename, clear, resume, or submit turns.
plugin: Experimental function hooks expose controlled session operations and a callback command for approved automation.

ask: Users want MCP processes loaded only when a relevant skill needs them.
plugin: A skill and MCP manager start and stop servers on demand, with connection diagnostics.

ask: Users want built-in skills and reports usable in other languages.
plugin: An output style and localized skill pack provide translated guidance and reporting.

ask: Users want a web optimization audit and fix workflow.
plugin: A skill combines SEO, GEO, and AEO checks with project-specific remediation.

ask: Users want tasks synchronized across Notion and GitHub.
plugin: An MCP-backed skill tracks issue status, ownership, and linked changes across both services.

ask: Users want written dates and weekdays checked for consistency.
plugin: A Stop hook parses dates in the draft, calculates the weekday, and asks Claude to correct mismatches.

ask: Users want a notification when a session finishes or needs attention.
plugin: Notification and Stop hooks send configurable desktop or mobile alerts with the session identity.

ask: Users want project instructions reviewed and updated as knowledge changes.
plugin: A maintenance skill audits CLAUDE.md and linked notes against recent changes, proposes edits, and preserves provenance.

ask: Users want to source skills from remote endpoints.
plugin: An MCP or bin fetcher reads remote skill indexes, verifies sources, and installs namespaced local copies.

ask: Users want quick side questions without disturbing the main workflow.
plugin: A command invokes a focused helper with the current context and stores its answer for later retrieval.

ask: Users want a direct slash entry point for tools and multi-step workflows.
plugin: A command parses tool arguments and dispatches an approved tool or bundled skill sequence.

ask: Users want generated code and comments cleaned of filler.
plugin: A review skill checks changed code for unnecessary comments and rewrites the diff without changing behavior.

ask: Users want event color metadata in Google Workspace results.
plugin: An MCP tool wrapper returns the Google Calendar colorId field when detailed events are requested.

ask: Users want output styles mechanically enforced.
plugin: A Stop hook validates the draft against a schema or style rules and requests a corrected response.

ask: Users want plugin-provided terminal controls and panels.
plugin: Experimental function hooks register focused overlays, actions, and keybindings for plugin workflows.
